scoring._comment: Rewritten 2026-07-26 because the old rubric picked an NVIDIA simulation SDK over the launch of Opus 5. It rewarded 'novelty', which an LLM reads as obscurity, and 'magnitude', which a 5-hours-to-2-minutes speedup satisfies perfectly. Both pushed the account toward developer tooling nobody outside the industry can recognise. What replaces them is weighted on whether a stranger knows what the subject IS, and on an artefact rather than a feeling: the run has to write the actual message someone would send with the post, and the gate reads it.

_criteria.recognition: Would someone who does not work in technology recognise the subject AND what happened to it, from the hook alone, with nothing explained? NVIDIA is recognised; 'Isaac medical physics simulation framework' is not. This is the criterion the account was failing.
_criteria.sendability: Not a feeling. Write the message someone would actually send with it, put it in the spec as `sendTest`, and read it back. If it needs a word like framework, SDK or inference, nobody sends it.
_criteria.stakes: Name the person it lands on in one sentence, without speculating. If you cannot, this is zero and the story is probably not one.
_criteria.timeliness: Is this what people are already talking about today? A new account has to enter conversations that exist, not invent new ones. This is the opposite of the old 'novelty'.
_criteria.sourceQuality: A lab's own announcement outranks coverage of it, provided the page can actually be fetched.

_vetoes: A release of developer tooling is not a story on its own: a framework, an SDK, a library, an API, model weights, a benchmark. It qualifies only when a REPORTED human consequence already exists.
A funding round or a valuation is not a story unless the money changes something a named person experiences.
A paper or preprint with nothing deployed is not a story.
Any story whose hook needs a definition to be understood is out, however large the number in it.
